batch.note: REGISTERED AT N = 60/ARM BY §2.1's FILL (2026-08-24). The pre-pilot effort sweep ran 27/27 and §2.1's operable-condition-match rule chose the compute condition — codex.reasoningEffort = low with N = 60 — priced at the sweep's own observed durations (batch 6.72 h, 9.3 % of the 72 h budget). N = 60 is the branch the registration itself prices and certifies: §5.6's Tier C size simulation, its observed-validity-gap power ladder, §2.1's dual-pricing table and §5.2's realised-n arithmetic are all stated at N = 60, so the registered batch runs at the N its own operating characteristics were demonstrated at. The order block below was re-derived at 60 rounds (ten whole Williams blocks, no tail, attained spreads (0, 1)) — a strictly cleaner balance than the 50-round port carry it replaces. §7 delta 7 has landed the DERIVATION: harness/batch.py holds no round count of its own and reads this block, derive_order(rounds) is the authority at any N, schedule() asserts the expansion attains the spreads PUBLISHED here rather than 019's (1, 1), and harness/tests/test_schedule.py re-runs the search at whatever round count this block names. The numbers below are 020's own, derived by that search at the REGISTERED 60 rounds (R2-6: this sentence still called them 019's 50-round carry after the fill had replaced them); re-pinning at another N would be `batch.py derive-schedule --rounds N` plus an edit of this block, and no constant in batch.py moves. Sequential, never parallel. The per-call timeout ceiling is an APPARATUS bound: a call that reaches it is pipeline-invalid, excluded from every rate's denominator and reported with its own rate, and a per-arm timeout rate above timeoutRateCap is a control-gate failure adjudicating R1 in neither direction. The wrapper reads callTimeoutSeconds and timeoutKillAfterSeconds from HERE, so the registry, the driver and the wrapper cannot hold three ceilings; a harness test asserts these two values equal batch.py's constants.

order.construction: W1-W3 increment every symbol A->B->C->A per row; W4-W6 are those rows reversed
order.derivedBy: harness/batch.py derive_order(rounds=60), exhaustively over the 720 orderings of W1-W6 and the 30 ordered two-sequence tails, keeping the orders in which no arm ever immediately follows itself and returning the lexicographically-least of those minimizing (position spread, transition spread). The spreads above are what that search ATTAINED at this round count; §7 delta 7 publishes them because 019 asserted the pair (1, 1) as a floor, which is true at 50 rounds and wrong by construction at any other N.
order.note: 60 rounds of three arms: ten whole blocks of the six Williams sequences and NO tail, because 60 is a multiple of 6. 180 slots divide exactly over 3 positions, so the search attains position spread 0; 179 transitions do not divide over 6 ordered pairs, so the attained directed-transition spread is 1, with no arm ever immediately following itself. Those attained values are published above as data; harness/batch.py's schedule() requires the expansion to attain them EXACTLY, so a registry edited to a different count without a re-derivation fails the suite. Derived 2026-08-24 by `batch.py derive-schedule --rounds 60` after section 2.1's fill registered N = 60; the prior block carried Study 019's 50-round shape (8 blocks + a 2-sequence tail, spreads (1, 1)) as a port carry.

calibration.minimumViableProvenance: Maintainer's section 2a.4(2) declaration, 2026-08-25 (round 1, R1-17): declared AFTER the sweep fixed the compute condition (low) and BEFORE any pilot call, with batch.py pilot refusing while this member was null. Bound to the IDENTITY floor because section 5.7 registers arm A's imperfection as a reported result (019: A 0/38 perfect) — a perfect-rate minimum over all arms would abort by design. GO requires the derived one-sided 95% Clopper-Pearson lower bound of the identity-passing rate to reach 0.20 in EVERY arm, which at n=12 means at least 6/12 (floor 0.245; 5/12 floors at 0.181 and fails). Priced before the pilot: ~6% three-arm false-abort risk at 019's registered identity rates (0.895/0.703/0.718) versus ~19% at the next rung (>=7/12, min 0.30); a true rate of 1/3 (the C arm's swept n=3 point at low) is caught with probability 0.82. The abort is study-death under M-9 (no descope), so the gate catches COLLAPSE; thin-but-alive arms are section 2a.6's recomputed dispersion table's business. Full rationale in PREREGISTRATION.md section 2a.4's fill.
calibration.note: PREREGISTRATION.md section 2a. The pre-freeze pilot runs through harness/authoring_call.sh and harness/batch.py under the calibration mode `batch.py pilot` (PIN_LABEL=PILOT; round-1 finding R1-17), with output under calibration/<label>/arm-<ARM>/run-NNN and citable: false. The registered differences between the pilot and the primary batch are exactly four (section 2a.2) and the pilot slot count is one of them: as amended by round-2 finding R2-10 it names TWO numbers — pilotPerArm / scoredPerArm = 12 apparatus-clean calls per arm, the denominator section 2a.1's table prices the floor at, drawn from at most attemptCapPerArm = 21 attempts per arm. Every attempt is retained, sealed and published with its section 1a code; an arm short of 12 clean at the cap publishes no rates and is a DEVIATIONS.md event. At Study 019's own apparatus rates the probability that all three arms reach 12 clean within 12 attempts is ~0.0001, which is why the fixed-12 denominator made the 0.20 gate fire on apparatus noise about half the time; root is the subtree's registered name, read by the wrapper's slot-anchor gate. derivedFloor is emitted by calibration/derive_floor.py from the pilot's own per-arm counts by an exact Clopper-Pearson rule with no human number entering; minimumViable and minimumViableBasis are the maintainer's section 2a.4(2) declaration, made BEFORE the pilot runs and AFTER the sweep fixes the compute condition — batch.py pilot refuses while either is null, and derive_floor.py's go/no-go compares the DERIVED floors against the DECLARED minimum on the DECLARED basis (perfectFloor or identityFloor). The freeze gate PERMITS AND REQUIRES the calibration/ subtree (019 DEVIATIONS.md D-2) and, since round 2 (R2-7), AUTHENTICATES the pilot from its sealed, chained PILOT.json through batch.py's own readers — the round robin replayed from the records' own codes, the chain, every slot's seal against the record's digest, no slot the ledger does not name, every completed CALL.json's pin state (arm, slot index, PILOT label, citable: false, the ledger header's registry and golden digests, the pinned prompt and reasoning effort), and the rates record's rows exactly the ledger's slots with each cell reconciled to its rows; it still refuses any results/primary-attempt-*. The pilot runs the batch's own per-slot finalization (R2-8: refusal record, schedule stamps, transcript binding, seal, chained record, atomic ledger) and the golden capture is its precondition. ONE pilot, TERMINAL (section 2a.6 as amended, R2-12): there is no second pilot; a label under which no call completed is abandoned by `batch.py abandon --label` and retained under calibration/abandoned-<label>/. ROUND 2 (R2-11, R2-13): after the pilot and before the freeze, harness/pilot_analysis.py walks the sealed pilot slots ONCE and publishes calibration/<label>/C4-REFERENCE.json (the pilot side of section 2a.5's transfer gate — eight exact rows, two band rows under the R2-11(A) ruling, the reasoning-token median descriptive only) and calibration/<label>/PILOT-DISPERSION.json (section 2a.6's dispersion re-derived at the pinned effort: sigma per member on its registered basis, df, the exact chi-square 95% interval, MDE at the pilot's n and at the registered N; no contrast, no test, no direction — a no-peek gate refuses any such member at publication and at the freeze). c4ReferenceSha256 and dispersionSha256 pin them. ALL FIVE calibration members — label, outputSha256, derivedFloor, c4ReferenceSha256, dispersionSha256 — are FREEZE PINS since round 2: section 2a.6's 'label, N and output digest go into PINS.json before the primary attempt' was enforced by no label rule and study_label() returned REGISTERED with every one of them null.

registeredLabelRule: harness/integrity.py's study_label() labels a run REGISTERED only when EVERY pin the rule reads is filled, and the rule reads TWO tuples. FREEZE_PINS, twenty-three members: preregistration, policyProse, goldSuite, the three arm prompt digests (matrixA/matrixB/matrixC, stored at arms.<ARM>.promptSha256, the member the call wrapper's prompt-digest gate reads), mutantManifests, referenceA, referenceB, offGoldCertificate, studyManifest, opa.capabilitiesSha256 (opaCapabilities), jpack.reproducibleBuildAttestation (jpackBuildAttestation), probePrompt.sha256 (probePrompt), golden.sha256 (goldenContext), isolationNegative.assent (isolationAssent) reviewerMutantSet.sha256 (reviewerMutantSet) and censusStimulus.count (censusStimulusCount), the last of which is new in 020 because section 5.1's E5 registers the census count as freeze-pinned and Study 019 registered the same stimulus while pinning no count; and, new in round 2, the five calibration pins section 2a.6 registers as going into PINS.json before the primary attempt — calibration.label (calibrationLabel), calibration.outputSha256 (calibrationOutput), calibration.derivedFloor (calibrationDerivedFloor), calibration.c4ReferenceSha256 (c4Reference) and calibration.dispersionSha256 (pilotDispersion) — which no label rule read before round 2, so a REGISTERED attempt was reachable with the pilot unpinned. DESIGN_TIME_PINS, two members and NEW IN 020 under ruling M-25: codex.model (model) and codex.reasoningEffort (reasoningEffort). Study 019 carried codex.model as a freeze pin; it moves here because the compute condition is an OUTPUT of the pre-pilot sweep, which runs before the freeze, and a value the pre-freeze sweep must produce cannot be a value the freeze fills. The move is not a relaxation: a null in either design-time pin labels the run PILOT exactly as a null freeze pin does, and a PILOT supports no claim. The non-null members are enforced under both labels: a design-time resolved toolchain digest is checked whether or not the freeze has happened. ONE exemption is registered, one value and one label wide: under the --sweep label codex.reasoningEffort ALONE is exempt from the null check, because the sweep is the registered procedure that resolves it; codex.model is never exempt, every sweep call stamps its setting into its own CALL.json, and the sweep's outputs are citable: false and outside every population. harness/tests/test_pins.py drives the rule pin by pin: each member nulled alone on an otherwise-full registry must produce PILOT, and the sweep exemption must hold for exactly one pin and exactly one label. THE DESIGN-TIME HALF IS ALSO A GATE ON THE CALL, and it is a different rule with a different consequence: the pins section 2 marks resolvedAtDesignTime - codex.model, codex.reasoningEffort, codex.binarySha256, jpack.binarySha256, opa.assetSha256 - are checked WHETHER OR NOT THE FREEZE HAS HAPPENED, by harness/batch.py's require_design_time_pins(), which refuses the call rather than changing the label. codex.reasoningEffort ALONE is exempt under the --sweep label (harness/batch.py's SWEEP_EXEMPT_PINS and harness/integrity.py's SWEEP_EXEMPT_PINS name the same one member), the sweep still runs inside the harness, and nothing else is exempt at any label. NOTE, as a finding rather than a silence: Study 019 carried codex.model in FREEZE_PINS and section 2.1 rules it a design-time-resolved pin; ruling M-25 moves it, so it is in DESIGN_TIME_PINS and not in FREEZE_PINS here, and harness/tests/test_pins.py asserts the two tables do not overlap.

reviewerMutantSet.note: FRESH for this study (section 4.3). Study 019's set is SPENT - 019's own registry records 'first executed at the primary attempt' and 019's RESULTS.json publishes the outcome per run - so it does not carry and is kept only as a published comparison. 020's set is authored during review rounds, committed verbatim, freeze-pinned by digest, validated without execution before the attempt, first executed at the primary attempt under the mandatory --include-reviewer-set, executed exactly once, scored as authored, and reaching no member the decision reads. --include-reviewer-set refuses while any pin above is null.

sweep.abortRule: A setting whose FIRST arm-A call exceeds the registered per-call ceiling (batch.callTimeoutSeconds) is aborted after that call; a setting whose per-arm mean duration projects a primary batch beyond 72 h at the registered N branch is recorded as out of budget and is not swept further. Aborted settings are published with the call that aborted them.
sweep.budgetProjectionNote: The abort rule's second clause projects a primary batch 'beyond 72 h at the registered N branch'. At sweep time batch.n carried Study 019's round count as a PORT CARRY (section 7 delta 7), so the driver projected at 50 and RECORDED that branch in SWEEP.json (budgetProjectionNSource: batch.n); section 2.1's fill then registered N = 60, and batch.n now carries the registered count - a future driver run would project at 60. Over a registry with no count at all the projection falls to the ONE branch PREREGISTRATION.md section 2.1's dual-pricing table prices, N = 60/arm = 180 calls. The driver never silently picks the cheaper branch; it records which it used. budgetHours and budgetProjectionN are asserted equal to harness/batch.py's SWEEP_BUDGET_HOURS and SWEEP_BUDGET_PROJECTION_N by harness/tests/test_sweep.py.
sweep.chosenSettingNote: Section 2.1's fill, 2026-08-24: chosen by the operable-condition-match rule from the published sweep (sweeps/2026-08-24-effort-sweep) - the pinned model's own catalog default, the only tier condition-matched to Study 019's batch (section 2a.6), passing operability 9/9 with a 6.72 h projected batch at the registered N = 60 (the ledger's own projection line, printed at the then-carried batch.n = 50, reads 5.60 h). The rule reads registered facts and the sweep's operability columns; it deliberately does not read the published per-arm perfect and identity rates, because a tier chosen on n = 3 rates would be the picked-not-swept condition section 2.1 forbids. The rule's TEXT was named at fill time, as section 2.1 registered ('the chosen setting is named with the rule that chose it'); the fill says so plainly rather than implying the rule predates the sweep.

evidenceTrees.rule: sha256 over the sorted '<relpath> <sha256>' lines of every file under the named sweeps/ entry - R1-19: the section 2.1 fill's evidence is pinned per tree, harness/integrity.py verifies each named tree byte for byte (a mutated, added or deleted file fails), and a FUTURE sweeps/ entry is permitted by not being named rather than by weakening the pinned ones R2-15: the walk lstats EVERY entry and refuses a symlink (to a file or to a directory), a special file and an empty directory - none of which contributes a line, so each could have been added without moving the digest; the three pinned values do not move under the fence.

sweep.note: PREREGISTRATION.md section 2.1, rulings M-8/M-20/M-25. The pre-pilot effort sweep is n = 3/arm across three settings, run THROUGH the registered apparatus (harness/authoring_call.sh + harness/batch.py under --sweep, never outside the harness - running it outside is the 019 failure exactly). Its outputs are citable: false and outside every population. The registered compute condition - the codex.reasoningEffort value and the per-arm N together - is chosen from its result and priced at its own observed durations. The cap is not raised without a DEVIATIONS.md entry naming the reason and republishing the price.
sweep.noteOnTheModesName: The mode section 2.1 calls '--sweep' is the driver SUBCOMMAND harness/batch.py sweep - the subcommand form every other mode of this driver takes (plan, run, capture, capture-golden, capture-isolation-negative, shortfall) - and PIN_LABEL=SWEEP is what that mode claims at the wrapper. The name is reconciled in PREREGISTRATION.md section 2.1 under 'Where the set is carried, and the mode's name'; nothing about the exemption's width moves with it, and the wrapper still accepts the label from the driver and from nowhere else.
sweep.publication: The prereg's published-in-full obligation is discharged by two files under sweep.root: SWEEP.json, the machine-readable ledger (every call's setting, arm, run index, duration, completion bytes, reasoning_output_tokens where the transcript carries it, wrapper exit and refusal code, plus the per-setting abort verdicts and the M-24 witness branch), and SWEEP.md, the rendered per-setting per-arm table. Both are written for ABORTED settings too, carrying the call that aborted them, and both stamp citable: false on every row.
sweep.rootNote: The sweep's slot root, study-relative: sweeps/<UTC date>-effort-sweep/<setting>/arm-<ARM>/run-NNN. It is NOT arms/, and that is structural rather than an exception list: make_manifest.prior_authoring_problems() (R10-1) derives every path it refuses from authoring_state_paths(), which walks batch.slot_path() under batch.ARMS_ROOT, so a tree outside arms/ is outside that gate by construction - the same separation calibration/ has under section 2a.2. ADR 0004's exact-set manifest covers no byte under sweeps/ either, so require_lawful_destination() permits it. harness/batch.py owns the absolute constant (SWEEP_ROOT) and harness/tests/test_sweep.py asserts this member, that constant and make_manifest.SWEEP_ROOT are one spelling, and drives the occupancy gate in both directions.
sweep.settingsNote: REGISTERED 2026-08-24, BEFORE THE SWEEP, as the maintainer's decision - PREREGISTRATION.md section 2.1, 'The three swept settings'. The registered shape (3 settings x 3/arm) names a cardinality and no members, and a set whose members are chosen after the durations are seen is a picked set and not a swept one. The three are the pinned CLI's own named reasoning-effort tiers low, medium, high, in that order. The TODO this note once held open - the chosen condition, effort and per-arm N together - CLOSED with section 2.1's fill after the sweep ran: chosenSetting above, codex.reasoningEffort and batch.n carry it. Naming three tiers was not choosing one, and the record keeps the two moments distinct.
sweep.settingsProvenance: Measured 2026-08-24 against the pinned binary with no model call. (1) codex exec --help names no reasoning-effort flag; the spelling is the config override recorded under codex.reasoningEffortFlag / codex.reasoningEffortConfigKey. (2) codex debug models --bundled renders the catalog BAKED INTO the pinned binary - the only build-owned reading: over its EIGHT models the tier vocabulary is low, medium, high, xhigh, max, ultra; low/medium/high/xhigh are supported by 8/8, max by 3/8 and ultra by 2/8. (Provenance history, per round-1 finding R1-20: this member's first printing carried these same figures; a verification recount then 'corrected' them to 4/8 and medium x6 + high x1 by reading plain codex debug models, which renders a mutable post-call cache; the bundled recount restored the original figures and the preregistration's marked note records the lesson - build-owned means --bundled.) The swept set is the three LOWEST of the universally supported four, so it survives whichever model codex.model is pinned to. (3) Every model's own default_reasoning_level lies inside the set - low for gpt-5.6-sol, the model Study 019's batch ran, medium for the other seven - so the set contains the default 019's batch implicitly ran at and extends monotonically upward in cost. xhigh is as AVAILABLE as the three swept tiers, so its exclusion is a BUDGET decision and is registered as one, not passed off as an availability limit.
sweep.settingsUncapClause: xhigh, max and ultra are NOT swept and are reachable only by a DEVIATIONS.md entry naming the reason and republishing the price, under the same cap clause that governs raising callCap: reaching a costlier tier is the same act as buying more calls. harness/batch.py refuses a setting outside sweep.settings, and harness/authoring_call.sh refuses one too, so the deviation has to be written before either will run it.
